quote: Yeah. Yeah. This is a solar program they're offering that offers free installation.
stewart_read: Rep answers a cost/program-mechanics question definitively and without qualification before any verify items are run. 'Free installation' is a claim about program financing that belongs to the closer's proposal conversation, not an unqualified opener line.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be using scripted language Ion trains setters to say verbatim as a hook; if so this is schema-sanctioned, not scope creep. But nothing in the transcript shows the rep caveating or tying it to eligibility, so the claim lands as an unconditional promise.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to qualify any 'free installation' language with 'if you qualify' framing, and flag this exact promise to the closer so it doesn't create a credibility gap when the proposal shows program costs.

quote: Behind the home. The trees that were around the home, I got them cut down.
schema_reference: context (enthusiasm signals — tree removal improving sun exposure)
stewart_read: Customer proactively discloses she already removed trees that were shading the home — a concrete, unprompted improvement to solar viability that increases lead quality.
coaching_implication: Rep acknowledged it ('Okay. Great. Thanks for letting me know.') but never anchored it forward — e.g., tying it to system size or savings potential. Coach the rep to reflect these signals back as forward-pulling hooks rather than filing them.

quote: so they had to guesstimate me a bill. So they guesstimated me. It was a really high bill that they guesstimated. So I actually haven't even received my first my first bill yet.
stewart_read: Customer hands the rep a live, emotionally-charged billing complaint (a guessed bill she considers inflated) tied to a utility she's clearly annoyed with. This is exactly the kind of alignment-against-the-utility material objection_inversion is built for, but the rep does not flip it into urgency or savings framing.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the number unreliable (customer herself disavows it as 'not a real bill') and chose not to anchor on unverified data — a defensible restraint given numeric_discipline. This is the more supported read given the customer's explicit disavowal.
coaching_implication: Rather than using the $1,000 figure as leverage, the rep should have flagged the pending corrected bill as something to collect before or during the closer appointment — a process move, not a savings pitch built on a number the customer already said wasn't real.

quote: Okay. And who's the utility company?
stewart_read: Rep captures the utility name (Pepco) correctly per script, but the surrounding billing chaos (bypassed meter, incorrect readings, pending corrected bill) is a live open item that never gets a clear next step — no request for the corrected bill once received, no text/email follow-up instruction tied to it.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did pivot to square footage as a workaround (03:08), which is a reasonable adaptive substitute for a missing bill — this is not a total miss, but the corrected-bill thread is left dangling without a plan.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close the loop explicitly: 'once you get that corrected bill, text it to me or bring it to the appointment' — right now it's an open thread with no owner.

quote: Well, we can get a design started for this, 5,500.
stewart_read: With no usable bill on file, the rep adapts by using square footage as a proxy for system sizing — a reasonable substitute that keeps the call moving toward booking instead of stalling on the missing document.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would say the rep gave up on getting real usage data too easily. But given the customer explicitly has no valid bill yet (utility is redoing it), pursuing the bill further on this call would have been unproductive — the strategic read holds.
coaching_implication: This adaptation was fine for keeping the call moving, but the rep should still have set an explicit follow-up ask for the corrected bill before the appointment, not just substituted square footage as a permanent proxy.

quote: Alright. Sounds good. Thank you again. Yes. You're welcome. Talk to me. We'll see you this Wednesday, the twenty second at 9AM.
stewart_read: The rep restates the day/time correctly but never runs the 'is that fair?' handshake, never states the one-hour block, and never gives the no-driving/computer instruction before ending the call.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep did give a partial recap including duration ('It'll take, like, around thirty to forty five minutes') at 05:00, so button-up wasn't fully skipped — but the explicit verbal handshake and computer/no-driving instruction are absent.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always close with the explicit 'is that fair?' handshake and the no-driving/at-your-computer instruction — both are schema-required and both were skipped here despite an otherwise clean book.
